title: Design Add And Search Words Data Structure
description:
Build a dictionary of lowercase words and query it with patterns that may contain one-character wildcards.

Implement the WordDictionary class:

  • __init__() creates an empty dictionary.
  • addWord(word: str) -> None stores a complete word; repeats do not change whether a pattern matches.
  • search(word: str) -> bool tests a full-word pattern, where each dot matches exactly one lowercase letter.

The pattern must match the entire stored word: neither a prefix nor a suffix alone is enough. Dots do not match zero characters.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls on one live object. The first call names the class and passes constructor arguments; subsequent calls name methods and their arguments. The constructor and methods returning nothing report null; the result array has one entry per call.

Constraints:

  • Added words contain 1 to 25 lowercase English letters.
  • Queries contain 1 to 25 lowercase letters or dots.
  • At most 10000 calls; at most two dots per query.

Example 1:

Calls: ["WordDictionary","addWord","addWord","search","search","search"]
Arguments: [[],["bad"],["dad"],["pad"],[".ad"],["b.."]]
Output: [null,null,null,false,true,true]

pad is absent; .ad and b.. each match a whole stored three-letter word.

Example 2:

Calls: ["WordDictionary","addWord","search","search","search"]
Arguments: [[],["cat"],["ca"],["c.t"],["...."]]
Output: [null,null,false,true,false]

A prefix and a four-character pattern cannot match cat, but c.t can.

Example 3:

Calls: ["WordDictionary","search","addWord","search","search"]
Arguments: [[],["a"],["a"],["."],[".."]]
Output: [null,false,null,true,false]

Searching before the insertion fails; the single dot then matches the new one-letter word, but two dots need two letters.

The wildcard matches exactly one character and an is only a prefix.
A suffix alone is not a match.
Either stored middle letter may satisfy the dot.
Two dots match a two-letter word, not a one-letter word.
Repeating a word does not change exact or wildcard searches.
The final wildcard works; no stored word ends in e.
